title: Intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG) enriched with IgM attenuates multi-organ dysfunction in porcine fecal peritonitis sepsis
authors: Berlot, G., Biloslavo, S., Lucangelo, U., et al.
abstract:
Background: IgM-enriched immunoglobulins possess enhanced bacterial opsonization properties. We evaluated IgM-enriched IVIG in a clinically relevant porcine fecal peritonitis model.
Methods: Female domestic pigs received an intraperitoneal injection of autologous fecal slurry (1 g/kg) to elicit severe polymicrobial peritonitis. At the onset of arterial hypotension (MAP < 60 mmHg), swine received IgM-enriched IVIG (Pentaglobin, 250 mg/kg) or 5% human albumin infusion alongside fluid resuscitation and noradrenaline. Hemodynamics, blood lactate, and extravascular lung water index were monitored for 24 hours.
Results: Pigs receiving IgM-enriched IVIG had significantly lower noradrenaline requirements, attenuated acute lung injury scores, and faster lactate clearance (p < 0.05).
Conclusion: Early rescue administration of IgM-enriched immunoglobulin reduces vasopressor dependency and organ injury in porcine fecal peritonitis.
rationale: Clear include: In vivo swine, approved fecal peritonitis model, evaluates therapeutic intervention (IgM-enriched IVIG), published in 2021.
learning_pearl: Large mammal fecal peritonitis testing IVIG = Ideal include!

title: Lipopolysaccharide and D-galactosamine-induced acute liver failure in mice: Hepatoprotective mechanisms of silibinin
authors: Fang, L., Wu, J., Zhang, C.
abstract:
Background: Fulminant hepatic failure carries high clinical mortality. We examined silibinin in an LPS/D-GalN-induced acute liver injury model.
Methods: Female Balb/c mice were co-injected intraperitoneally with LPS (10 μg/kg) and D-galactosamine (700 mg/kg). Silibinin (100 mg/kg) was gavaged 1 hour prior. Serum ALT/AST, hepatic caspase-3, and TUNEL apoptosis were measured at 6 hours.
Results: Silibinin significantly reduced serum ALT elevation and suppressed hepatocyte apoptotic death.
Conclusions: Silibinin prevents LPS/D-GalN hepatotoxicity by suppressing apoptotic pathways.
rationale: Model violation: LPS + D-galactosamine challenge model. Pure endotoxin models are excluded under EX-LPS.
learning_pearl: LPS + D-galactosamine is an endotoxin hepatotoxicity model: EX-LPS!

title: Pre-treatment with resveratrol alleviates acute lung injury and suppresses HMGB1 release in rat cecal ligation and puncture
authors: Kovaleva, O., Smirnova, T., Petrov, A., et al.
abstract:
Background: Sepsis-induced acute lung injury is propagated by late inflammatory mediators such as high mobility group box 1 (HMGB1). We investigated prophylactic resveratrol in septic rats.
Methods: Sprague-Dawley rats received resveratrol (30 mg/kg/day orally) for 5 days preceding medium-grade CLP. Arterial oxygenation, lung wet-to-dry ratios, serum HMGB1, and lung histology were assessed 24 hours post-CLP.
Results: Rats pre-treated with resveratrol maintained significantly higher PaO2/FiO2 ratios (380 vs 210 mmHg, p < 0.001), had lower lung wet-to-dry ratios, and reduced circulating HMGB1 levels.
Conclusions: Prophylactic resveratrol preserves pulmonary barrier integrity in rat CLP sepsis.
rationale: Valid include: In vivo rats, approved CLP model, evaluates therapeutic intervention (resveratrol) administered prior to CLP. Guidelines state: interventions given before or after induction are included!
learning_pearl: Remember: Pre-induction administration is completely acceptable under our intervention criteria!

title: CRISPR-Cas9-mediated deletion of STING in mouse splenocytes suppresses bacterial phagocytosis ex vivo
authors: Harrington, P. E., Clark, S. J., Adams, M.
abstract:
Objective: To delineate the cell-autonomous role of STING in splenocyte antimicrobial defense.
Methods: Primary splenocytes harvested from healthy C57BL/6 mice were subjected to ex vivo electroporation with Cas9-gRNA ribonucleoprotein complexes targeting Sting1. Splenocytes were incubated in 24-well culture plates with GFP-labeled E. coli for 6 hours. Phagocytic uptake and cytokine secretion were analyzed by flow cytometry.
Results: STING-deficient splenocytes exhibited a 45% decline in bacterial internalization without changes in cell viability.
Conclusion: STING promotes optimal phagocytosis in cultured murine splenocytes.
rationale: Model violation: Ex vivo cultured splenocytes in culture plates. No whole animal sepsis model.
learning_pearl: Primary splenocytes cultured ex vivo without live animal experiments = EX-NOT-INVIVO.

title: Delayed resuscitation with synthetic high-density lipoprotein nanoparticles reduces mortality in murine colon ascendants stent peritonitis
authors: Goldberg, R. S., Nguyen, T. K., Sharma, P., et al.
abstract:
Background: Endogenous high-density lipoproteins neutralize microbial toxins during sepsis. We tested synthetic HDL nanoparticles (sHDL) in continuous fecal peritonitis.
Methods: Male C57BL/6 mice underwent CASP surgery. At 4 hours post-CASP, mice received IV sHDL nanoparticles (80 mg/kg) or vehicle control. Plasma endotoxin neutralizing capacity, bacteremia, organ histology, and 7-day survival were recorded.
Results: sHDL administration promoted bacterial toxin sequestration, reduced systemic cytokine storm, and elevated 7-day survival from 20% in vehicle controls to 65% (p = 0.002).
Conclusion: Synthetic HDL nanoparticles confer significant therapeutic protection in severe continuous polymicrobial sepsis.
rationale: Clear include: In vivo mice, approved CASP model, evaluates therapeutic intervention (sHDL nanoparticles) given post-induction, 2022 publication.
learning_pearl: Nanoparticle therapeutics evaluated in CASP sepsis are eligible inclusions.

title: Impact of hypertonic saline resuscitation on cerebral edema in experimental rat traumatic brain injury
authors: Duarte, J. C., Silva, F. B., Castro, E.
abstract:
Background: Severe traumatic brain injury (TBI) results in cytotoxic brain edema. We assessed hypertonic saline (3% NaCl) in a fluid percussion injury model.
Methods: Sprague-Dawley rats underwent controlled fluid percussion brain trauma. Rats received 3% NaCl or normal saline IV at 30 min post-injury. Intracranial pressure (ICP) and brain water content were assessed.
Results: Hypertonic saline lowered elevated ICP and improved motor coordination scores.
Conclusions: Hypertonic saline effectively reduces cerebral edema after blunt trauma.
rationale: Condition violation: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) is a sterile trauma model, not a sepsis model.
learning_pearl: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) without sepsis is excluded under EX-NOT-SEPSIS.

title: Therapeutic efficacy of aerosolized colistin in a murine model of multidrug-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii pneumonia-induced sepsis
authors: Choi, M. J., Kang, S. H., Park, C. W., et al.
abstract:
Objectives: Pneumonia-derived sepsis caused by MDR Acinetobacter baumannii has high clinical mortality. We assessed inhaled versus intravenous colistin in mice.
Methods: BALB/c mice received intranasal inoculation of live A. baumannii (10^8 CFU) to produce necrotizing pneumonia and secondary bacteremic sepsis. At 6 hours post-inoculation, mice received aerosolized colistin (5 mg/kg), IV colistin, or saline twice daily for 3 days. Bacterial burdens in lung and spleen, arterial blood gas, and 7-day survival were determined.
Results: Inhaled colistin cleared pulmonary and systemic bacterial dissemination faster than IV colistin and improved 7-day survival from 15% to 75% (p < 0.001).
Conclusions: Inhaled colistin provides potent local and systemic therapeutic efficacy in pneumonia-derived sepsis.
rationale: Clear include: In vivo mice, approved pneumonia-derived sepsis model (intranasal inoculation with live pathogen causing systemic sepsis), evaluates therapeutic colistin, published in 2023.
learning_pearl: Intranasal inoculation with live pathogens causing systemic sepsis is an approved model!

title: In vitro evaluation of silver nanoparticles against clinical bacterial isolates
authors: Rao, K. S., Venkat, A., Reddy, M.
abstract:
Background: Nanotechnology offers innovative antimicrobials. We evaluated the minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) of silver nanoparticles against 50 hospital isolates of E. coli and P. aeruginosa in microtiter plates. Zone of inhibition assays and scanning electron microscopy demonstrated membrane disruption without testing animals.
Conclusion: Silver nanoparticles possess strong broad-spectrum antibacterial properties in broth cultures.
rationale: Model violation: Broth microdilution in vitro assays only. No animal models used.
learning_pearl: In vitro broth microdilution assays without animal models = EX-NOT-INVIVO.

title: Protective effects of erythropoietin against multi-organ dysfunction in rat cecal ligation and puncture
authors: Mitaka, C., Hirata, Y., Yokoyama, K., et al.
abstract:
Objective: Non-erythropoietic actions of erythropoietin include anti-apoptotic and anti-inflammatory effects. We tested recombinant human erythropoietin (rhEPO) in rat CLP.
Methods: Male Wistar rats underwent CLP. rhEPO (1000 U/kg) or saline was injected IV 1 hour after CLP. Serum TNF-alpha, creatinine, and 48-hour survival were recorded.
Results: rhEPO significantly decreased serum creatinine and improved 48-hour survival (65% vs 30%).
Conclusion: rhEPO protects against organ dysfunction in septic rats.
rationale: Date violation: Published in 2016. Our protocol limits inclusion to studies published from 2020 to present.
learning_pearl: Always check the date: 2016 is before the 2020 limit, so exclude under EX-PRE2020.

title: Cecum and colon ligation with dissection (CCLD): A modified surgical peritonitis model in swine treated with methylene blue
authors: Lang, M. D., Cooper, T. J., Harrison, P. W., et al.
abstract:
Objective: Cecum and colon ligation with dissection (CCLD) models fulminant bowel necrosis and fecal peritonitis in large animals. We tested the nitric oxide scavenger methylene blue.
Methods: Anesthetized Yorkshire swine underwent CCLD surgery. At the onset of vasoplegic refractory shock, swine received an intravenous bolus of methylene blue (2 mg/kg) followed by continuous infusion or vehicle saline. Vasopressor requirements, oxygen consumption, and mesenteric lactate flux were recorded.
Results: Swine receiving methylene blue exhibited rapid restoration of mean arterial pressure, a 60% reduction in norepinephrine dosage, and improved intestinal oxygen extraction.
Conclusions: Methylene blue is an effective rescue adjunct in large-animal surgical peritonitis.
rationale: Clear include: In vivo swine, approved surgical variant (cecum/colon ligation and dissection CCLD), evaluates therapeutic intervention (methylene blue), published in 2022.
learning_pearl: Cecum/colon ligation and dissection variants in swine are explicitly included!

title: Lipopolysaccharide-induced cognitive impairment in mice is attenuated by epigallocatechin gallate
authors: Li, Y., Zhou, X., Chen, Z.
abstract:
Background: Systemic administration of LPS elicits neuroinflammation and memory deficits. We assessed green tea polyphenol EGCG in LPS-treated mice.
Methods: C57BL/6 mice were injected intraperitoneally with LPS (1 mg/kg/day) for 7 days. EGCG (50 mg/kg/day) was administered orally. Morris water maze tests and hippocampal microglial activation were measured.
Results: EGCG treatment improved spatial memory retention and lowered hippocampal TNF-alpha.
Conclusion: EGCG alleviates LPS-induced cognitive dysfunction and neuroinflammation.
rationale: Model violation: Repeated intraperitoneal LPS injection model. Excluded under EX-LPS.
learning_pearl: Systemic LPS-induced neuroinflammation is an LPS model: EX-LPS.

title: Therapeutic administration of antimicrobial peptide LL-37 enhances bacterial clearance and improves survival in murine Candida albicans candidemia
authors: Macedo, D. T., Barboza, R., Santos, D. A., et al.
abstract:
Background: Fungal sepsis caused by Candida species carries mortality exceeding 40%. We evaluated whether therapeutic administration of cathelicidin LL-37 improves clearance during systemic candidemia.
Methods: Female C57BL/6 mice were inoculated intravenously with live Candida albicans (1x10^5 CFU) to produce systemic candidemia and fungal sepsis. Mice received LL-37 (5 mg/kg IV) or vehicle control at 6 and 24 hours post-infection. Kidney fungal burdens, serum beta-glucan, and 14-day survival were assessed.
Results: LL-37 treatment accelerated fungal clearance in renal tissue by 2.1 log10 CFU/g, lowered serum beta-glucan levels, and increased 14-day survival from 20% to 65% (p = 0.003).
Conclusions: LL-37 provides potent antifungal efficacy and survival benefits in live-pathogen fungal sepsis.
rationale: Clear include: In vivo mice, live Candida pathogen causing systemic candidemia/fungal sepsis, therapeutic intervention (LL-37), 2023 publication.
learning_pearl: Live fungal pathogens (Candida) paired with systemic candidemia/sepsis are eligible!

title: Oleic acid-induced acute respiratory distress syndrome in sheep: Effects of prone positioning on gas exchange
authors: Pellegrini, M., Hedenstierna, G., Larsson, A.
abstract:
Background: Acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) disrupts oxygenation. We tested prone positioning in an ovine oleic acid ARDS model.
Methods: Mechanically ventilated sheep received intravenous oleic acid (0.08 mL/kg) to induce sterile chemical capillary leak and pulmonary edema. Sheep were randomized to prone versus supine ventilation for 6 hours. PaO2/FiO2 and CT density were recorded.
Results: Prone positioning significantly improved dorsal alveolar recruitment and PaO2/FiO2 ratio.
Conclusion: Prone positioning improves oxygenation in non-septic oleic acid pulmonary injury.
rationale: Condition violation: Oleic acid produces sterile chemical fat-embolism lung injury without infection or sepsis.
learning_pearl: Oleic acid is a classic sterile ARDS model, not sepsis: EX-NOT-SEPSIS.

title: Agar pellet implantation model of Bacteroides fragilis and Escherichia coli abdominal sepsis in rats: Therapeutic impact of metronidazole and ceftriaxone
authors: Kassianos, G., Papavramidis, T. S., Kotzampassi, K.
abstract:
Background: Agar pellet encapsulation permits sustained, localized bacterial release simulating perforated appendicitis abscesses. We evaluated metronidazole plus ceftriaxone in this polymicrobial model.
Methods: Wistar rats received intraperitoneal implantation of a standardized agar pellet containing live Bacteroides fragilis (10^8 CFU) and E. coli (10^7 CFU). Twelve hours later, rats received intraperitoneal metronidazole (30 mg/kg) and ceftriaxone (50 mg/kg) or vehicle control for 5 days. Abscess formation, blood bacteremia, and survival were recorded.
Results: Antibiotic treatment eliminated systemic bacteremia, contained abscess encapsulation, and improved 7-day survival from 25% to 80% (p < 0.001).
Conclusions: Combination antimicrobial therapy effectively treats polymicrobial agar pellet peritonitis.
rationale: Clear include: In vivo rats, approved agar pellet implantation model with live pathogens, therapeutic antibiotic intervention, 2020 publication.
learning_pearl: Agar pellet implantation models are explicitly listed in our criteria!

title: Global incidence and mortality of sepsis: A systematic review and meta-analysis of observational studies
authors: Rudd, K. E., Johnson, S. C., Agesa, K. M., et al.
abstract:
Background: Sepsis is a major cause of health loss globally. We estimated global, regional, and national sepsis incidence and mortality from 1990 to 2017 using vital statistics and hospital records from the Global Burden of Diseases Study.
Findings: An estimated 48.9 million incident cases of sepsis and 11.0 million sepsis-related deaths occurred worldwide in 2017, representing 19.7% of all global deaths.
Interpretation: Sepsis remains an immense public health burden worldwide.
rationale: Design violation: Epidemiological systematic review of human global burden data, not primary animal intervention research.
learning_pearl: Epidemiological syntheses and meta-analyses are excluded under EX-NONPRIMARY.

title: Neonatal sepsis induced by Streptococcus agalactiae in newborn C57BL/6 mice: Protection conferred by human milk oligosaccharide 2'-fucosyllactose
authors: Freitas, C. M., Silva, E. P., Duarte, M. S., et al.
abstract:
Background: Newborns are highly vulnerable to Group B Streptococcus (S. agalactiae) septicemia. We examined the therapeutic efficacy of human milk oligosaccharide 2'-fucosyllactose (2'-FL).
Methods: Seven-day-old C57BL/6 mouse pups were infected intraperitoneally with live Streptococcus agalactiae (10^6 CFU) to establish neonatal sepsis. Pups received oral 2'-FL (100 mg/kg) or vehicle at 2 and 12 hours post-infection. Blood bacterial burden, spleen CFU, serum cytokines, and 5-day survival were recorded.
Results: Pups receiving 2'-FL exhibited a 2.5-log reduction in systemic bacteremia, reduced circulating TNF-alpha, and significantly higher 5-day survival (72% vs 28%, p = 0.004).
Conclusion: Oral administration of 2'-FL confers potent therapeutic protection in neonatal streptococcal sepsis.
rationale: Clear include: In vivo newborn mouse pups, approved neonatal sepsis / Streptococcus agalactiae model, evaluates therapeutic intervention (2'-FL), 2022 publication.
learning_pearl: Neonatal mouse pups with live Streptococcus sepsis are eligible!

title: Therapeutic targeting of pyroptosis with MCC950 in Drosophila melanogaster infected with Pseudomonas aeruginosa
authors: Dumont, F., Lefebvre, P., Roux, M.
abstract:
Background: Drosophila melanogaster possesses an innate immune signaling cascade homologous to mammalian Toll pathways. We tested NLRP3 inhibitor MCC950 in fruit flies.
Methods: Adult female D. melanogaster flies were inoculated with live P. aeruginosa via septic needle injury. Flies were fed MCC950 (10-50 μM) or vehicle in sucrose food. Survival was monitored over 7 days.
Results: MCC950 supplementation extended fly median survival by 48 hours and dampened antimicrobial peptide expression.
Conclusion: Small molecule inflammasome inhibitors extend lifespan in infected Drosophila.
rationale: Organism violation: Drosophila melanogaster (fruit flies) are non-mammalian insects. Excluded under EX-NOT-INVIVO.
learning_pearl: Fruit flies (Drosophila) are non-mammalian models: EX-NOT-INVIVO.

title: Polymicrobial intra-abdominal sepsis in pigs: Protective effects of early peritoneal dialysis with icodextrin on renal perfusion
authors: Thooft, A., Favory, R., Salgado, D. R., et al.
abstract:
Purpose: Peritoneal sepsis frequently triggers septic acute kidney injury. We evaluated the therapeutic effect of early continuous peritoneal dialysis (PD) with icodextrin in swine.
Materials and Methods: Anesthetized domestic pigs underwent surgical cecal perforation to establish intra-abdominal polymicrobial peritonitis. At 4 hours post-induction, pigs received either PD with 7.5% icodextrin solution or sham peritoneal catheterization. Renal cortical blood flow (laser Doppler), urine output, and creatinine clearance were tracked for 24 hours.
Results: PD-treated pigs maintained higher renal cortical microperfusion, sustained urine output, and exhibited lower systemic lactate levels compared to sham controls (p < 0.05).
Conclusions: Peritoneal dialysis with icodextrin provides renal microcirculatory protection in porcine polymicrobial peritonitis.
rationale: Clear include: In vivo swine, approved polymicrobial abdominal peritonitis model (cecal perforation), evaluates therapeutic peritoneal dialysis, 2020 publication.
learning_pearl: Supportive and organ replacement interventions (like peritoneal dialysis) tested in sepsis models are included!

title: Lipopolysaccharide challenge in pregnant sheep induces fetal inflammatory response syndrome
authors: Kemp, M. W., Saito, M., Usuda, H., et al.
journal: American Journal of Obstetrics and Gynecology
abstract:
Objective: Intra-amniotic inflammation leads to preterm delivery and lung remodeling. We characterized fetal responses to intra-amniotic LPS.
Methods: Chronically catheterized pregnant Merino ewes received intra-amniotic injection of E. coli LPS (10 mg) at 120 days gestation. Animals were sacrificed 48 hours later. Fetal blood cytokines, lung histology, and amniotic fluid inflammatory cells were examined without testing therapies.
Results: LPS challenge induced massive fetal neutrophilic infiltration and elevated amniotic IL-6 and IL-8.
Conclusions: Intra-amniotic LPS reliably replicates fetal inflammatory response syndrome in sheep.
rationale: Model violation: Pure intra-amniotic LPS injection endotoxin model; also did not test a therapeutic candidate.
learning_pearl: Pure LPS injection models are excluded under EX-LPS.

title: Therapeutic administration of recombinant human thrombomodulin preserves gut mucosal barrier in murine cecal ligation and puncture
authors: Takahashi, G., Matsumoto, N., Shibata, S., et al.
abstract:
Background: Intestinal epithelial hyperpermeability fuels systemic bacterial translocation in sepsis. We evaluated recombinant human thrombomodulin (rhTM) on gut mucosal barrier function.
Methods: Male C57BL/6 mice were subjected to CLP. Animals received rhTM (3 mg/kg IP) or saline at 2 hours and 12 hours post-surgery. Gut mucosal permeability to FITC-dextran, ileal mucosal zonula occludens-1 (ZO-1) staining, and 7-day survival were assessed.
Results: rhTM significantly reduced luminal FITC-dextran leak into systemic blood, preserved ileal tight junction architecture, and improved 7-day survival from 30% to 70% (p = 0.008).
Conclusion: Post-treatment with rhTM protects gut mucosal barrier integrity and improves survival in polymicrobial peritonitis.
rationale: Clear include: In vivo mice, approved CLP model, therapeutic intervention (rhTM) administered after induction, 2022 publication.
learning_pearl: Post-induction administration of rhTM in CLP is fully eligible!

title: Effects of hyperoxia on ventilator-induced lung injury in rabbits without bacterial infection
authors: Mueller-Redetzky, H. C., Suttorp, N., Witzenrath, M.
abstract:
Background: High oxygen fractions are commonly delivered during critical care. We evaluated 100% FiO2 during mechanical ventilation in rabbits.
Methods: Anesthetized rabbits were ventilated for 6 hours with 100% O2 or 21% O2 under moderate tidal volumes without any infectious or surgical sepsis insult. Pulmonary histology, protein in bronchoalveolar lavage fluid, and lung compliance were assessed.
Results: Hyperoxia combined with mechanical ventilation aggravated alveolar-capillary barrier permeability.
Conclusion: Hyperoxia exacerbates non-infectious ventilator-induced lung injury.
rationale: Condition violation: Sterile hyperoxic ventilator-induced lung injury without sepsis.
learning_pearl: Non-infectious ventilator injury is not sepsis: EX-NOT-SEPSIS.

title: Therapeutic evaluation of bacteriophage therapy in murine Klebsiella pneumoniae bloodstream infection and sepsis
authors: Singla, S., Harjai, K., Chhibber, S.
journal: Frontiers in Cellular and Infection Microbiology
abstract:
Background: Multi-drug resistant Gram-negative bacteremia requires alternative therapies. We tested a specific lytic bacteriophage (KPO1K2) in bloodstream sepsis.
Methods: Female BALB/c mice were injected intravenously with live Klebsiella pneumoniae (10^8 CFU) to establish acute bacteremic sepsis. At 3 hours post-infection, mice received a single intraperitoneal dose of phage KPO1K2 (10^9 PFU) or heat-inactivated phage control. Blood bacterial counts, organ histopathology, and 10-day survival were monitored.
Results: Phage administration reduced blood bacterial counts to below detection limits within 24 hours, resolved splenic necrosis, and yielded 90% survival compared to 10% in control animals (p < 0.001).
Conclusions: Bacteriophage rescue is highly effective against live-pathogen bloodstream sepsis in vivo.
rationale: Clear include: In vivo mice, approved live-pathogen bloodstream infection / sepsis model, evaluates therapeutic bacteriophage intervention, 2020 publication.
learning_pearl: Bacteriophage therapy in live Klebsiella bloodstream sepsis is an ideal include!

title: Caenorhabditis elegans as an infection model to identify antimicrobial flavonoids against Staphylococcus aureus
authors: Kong, C., Yehye, W. A., Abd Rahman, N., et al.
abstract:
Introduction: Caenorhabditis elegans is widely employed as a whole-organism invertebrate model for antifungal and antibacterial drug discovery.
Methods: Nematodes were fed live S. aureus in 96-well plates and incubated with synthetic flavonoid derivatives (10-100 μM). Worm motility and lifespan were determined.
Results: Compound FL-4 significantly extended nematode survival during bacterial gut colonization.
Conclusion: C. elegans provides a tractable model for screening antibacterial small molecules.
rationale: Organism violation: Caenorhabditis elegans (nematodes) are invertebrate worms, not mammals. Excluded under EX-NOT-INVIVO.
learning_pearl: Nematodes (C. elegans) are non-mammalian organisms: EX-NOT-INVIVO.

title: Therapeutic administration of hydrogen-rich saline improves survival and decreases renal cell apoptosis in rat cecal ligation and incision
authors: Shi, Q., Zhang, P., Wang, K., et al.
abstract:
Background: Cecal ligation and incision (CLI) generates aggressive peritonitis. We investigated whether therapeutic hydrogen-rich saline (HRS) attenuates acute kidney injury.
Methods: Male Sprague-Dawley rats underwent CLI surgery. HRS (5 mL/kg IP) or normal saline was injected 2 hours and 12 hours post-surgery. Serum creatinine, renal tubular injury scores, caspase-3 expression, and 7-day survival were assessed.
Results: HRS-treated rats showed lower serum creatinine, reduced renal tubular vacuolization and apoptosis, and increased 7-day survival from 22% to 58% (p = 0.012).
Conclusion: Delayed administration of hydrogen-rich saline confers therapeutic renoprotection in experimental polymicrobial peritonitis.
rationale: Clear include: In vivo rats, approved CLI variant (cecal ligation and incision), evaluates therapeutic intervention (hydrogen-rich saline), 2023 publication.
learning_pearl: Cecal ligation and incision (CLI) is an approved surgical variant of CLP!

title: Evaluation of botanical extracts against septic peritonitis in French language publication
authors: Dupond, J., Martin, L., Bernard, C.
abstract:
Resume: Nous avons evalue l'efficacite de l'extrait de Thymus vulgaris chez le rat soumis a une ligature et ponction caecale (CLP). L'extrait administre par voie orale a ameliore modestement la survie globale des animaux.
Conclusion: Les extraits de thym presentent des activites antibacteriennes interessantes.
rationale: Language violation: Published in French. Our protocol limits our search to English-language publications.
learning_pearl: Non-English publications are excluded under EX-LANG.

title: Delayed administration of recombinant human alkaline phosphatase attenuates renal microvascular shutdown in rat fecal-induced peritonitis
authors: Peters, E., Heemskerk, S., Masereeuw, R., et al.
abstract:
Background: Alkaline phosphatase dephosphorylates and detoxifies bacterial endotoxins and purinergic ATP. We evaluated recombinant human alkaline phosphatase (recAP) in rat fecal peritonitis.
Methods: Wistar rats were injected intraperitoneally with autologous cecal fecal slurry (FIP model). At 3 hours post-injection, rats received IV recAP (1000 U/kg) or vehicle saline. Renal cortical sidestream dark-field microcirculation, glomerular filtration, and urinary kidney injury molecule-1 (KIM-1) were tracked.
Results: recAP preserved renal cortical capillary perfusion, suppressed urinary KIM-1 leakage, and improved creatinine clearance (p < 0.01).
Conclusions: recAP is an effective therapeutic candidate for sepsis-induced acute kidney injury.
rationale: Clear include: In vivo rats, approved Fecal-Induced Peritonitis (FIP) model, evaluates therapeutic intervention (recAP), 2021 publication.
learning_pearl: Therapeutic alkaline phosphatase in FIP peritonitis is fully eligible!

title: Lipopolysaccharide challenge in RAW 264.7 cells: Anti-inflammatory profiling of flavonoid derivatives
authors: Kim, H. J., Lee, S. J., Park, J. H.
abstract:
Summary: Murine RAW 264.7 macrophages were exposed to LPS (1 μg/mL) with or without synthetic flavonoids. Nitric oxide (NO) production, inducible nitric oxide synthase (iNOS) protein, and COX-2 levels were determined by Western blotting and Griess assay without animal experiments.
Conclusion: Synthetic flavonoids suppress NO production in vitro.
rationale: Model violation: In vitro RAW 264.7 cell culture assay only. Excluded under EX-NOT-INVIVO.
learning_pearl: Macrophage cell line testing in petri dishes is EX-NOT-INVIVO.

title: Therapeutic administration of monoclonal anti-TNF antibody in combination with meropenem in murine polymicrobial peritonitis
authors: Evans, T. J., Morrison, D., Hughes, J.
abstract:
Background: Co-administration of targeted immunomodulators with bactericidal antibiotics may improve sepsis survival. We tested anti-TNF mAb plus meropenem.
Methods: C57BL/6 mice underwent CLP peritonitis. Mice received combination therapy with anti-TNF monoclonal antibody (200 μg IP) and meropenem (20 mg/kg SC) or meropenem monotherapy starting 4 hours post-CLP. Systemic bacteremia, peritoneal cytokine levels, and 7-day survival were recorded.
Results: Combination therapy dampened hyperinflammatory cytokine spikes without impairing bacterial killing, significantly improving 7-day survival over monotherapy (75% vs 45%, p = 0.015).
Conclusions: Co-administration of anti-TNF antibody alongside antibiotic therapy provides survival benefit in polymicrobial peritonitis.
rationale: Clear include: In vivo mice, approved CLP model, evaluates therapeutic intervention (anti-TNF mAb co-administered with antibiotic), 2023 publication. (Our guidelines state: 'Interventions co-administered with other treatments will also be included').
learning_pearl: Co-administered combinations (e.g., antibody + antibiotic) are explicitly included!

title: Intratracheal lipopolysaccharide challenge induces neutrophilic lung inflammation in mice
authors: Ting, C., Lin, F., Chen, B.
abstract:
Background: Endotoxin inhalation elicits prominent airway neutrophilia. We evaluated pulmonary cytokine kinetics after intratracheal LPS.
Methods: Male C57BL/6 mice received intratracheal administration of Pseudomonas LPS (50 μg). Mice were sacrificed at 4, 12, and 24 hours. Bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF) cell counts and histology were evaluated without testing therapies.
Results: Intratracheal LPS evoked a 10-fold surge in BALF neutrophils and elevated MIP-2.
Conclusions: Intratracheal LPS is a reproducible model of acute neutrophilic airway inflammation.
rationale: Model violation: Pure LPS challenge model (intratracheal LPS). Excluded under EX-LPS.
learning_pearl: Whether given IP, IV, or intratracheally, pure LPS challenge is excluded under EX-LPS.

title: Therapeutic efficacy of fecal microbiota transplantation in an agar pellet peritonitis model in rats
authors: Zhao, C., Zhang, W., Li, M., et al.
abstract:
Background: Disruptions of intestinal microbial diversity worsen outcomes in intra-abdominal sepsis. We evaluated therapeutic fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) in an agar pellet peritonitis model.
Methods: Wistar rats were implanted with an intraperitoneal agar pellet containing live E. coli and Enterococcus faecalis. Six hours after surgery, rats were gavaged with healthy donor fecal microbiota slurry or vehicle once daily for 3 days. Gut mucosal integrity, systemic bacteremia, and 7-day survival were determined.
Results: FMT restored microbial short-chain fatty acid concentrations, reduced bacterial translocation to the liver and spleen, and enhanced 7-day survival from 25% to 65% (p = 0.008).
Conclusion: Fecal microbiota transplantation is an effective therapeutic modality in experimental agar pellet peritonitis.
rationale: Clear include: In vivo rats, approved agar pellet peritonitis model, evaluates therapeutic intervention (FMT), 2023 publication.
learning_pearl: Agar pellet implantation model testing FMT is an eligible include!
